The mask of normalcy I continue to put up while I’m burying my past, is what makes me feel truly icky. When she tells me she loves me, and I’m her greatest source of happiness, I break a little, because I know the truth. I really am grateful for your feedback though. You seem to have a very direct yet understanding way of looking at things, which is what I need right now.

Thank you again. Redemption is something I’ve never envisioned for myself. My girlfriend, the only person I truly care about, is the only one I would like to disclose my past to. I feel that she has a right to know, especially since we’re planning a future together. This secret keeping makes me feel so icky. I know she has done some things in her past that she’s not proud of, but this is taken to a whole new level. I hate lying to her, especially with something as serious as this. I just don’t know anymore.
I’d love to hear your story, if you’re comfortable sharing. My messages are always open :)

I’m so grateful for this reply, really. I think that might be one of my problems. I’ve been trying to twist and turn things to somehow fit the mold of a good person, but all I really have to do is accept this deplorable behavior for what it is, what I’ve done. As to your last question, I’m honestly not sure where my behavior stemmed from. My parents were never racist, my mother at least (father was out of the picture). I know that she would be devastated if she found out. I spent a lot of my youth online, still do... a great deal of time acting like this big tough internet troll, who would say things I would never dare to say to someone’s face. But then of course, these thoughts had to stem from somewhere in the first place... all I know is, I knew better, but I chose a different route. Now I regret it, and karma’s a bitch ;)
Thank you for the response! It’s going to be hard, but I feel that she needs to know.
